title: Linux in a Tab
subtitle: How wasm-vm streams a disk, joins a tailnet, and freezes a machine

chapters.title: Only the Blocks You Touch
chapters.blurb: A 768 MB ext4 image cut into 6,144 content-addressed 128 KiB chunks, fetched and hash-verified one guest read at a time — 100 chunks reach a login prompt. Then the same manifest becomes a torrent scoped to your tailnet: the bucket demoted to web seed (R2 or S3 — the busier your swarm, the cheaper the seat), guest reads jumping the queue as critical pieces, and per-piece availability re-deriving the boot profile.

chapters.title: The Tab Is the Node
chapters.blurb: Unmodified Alpine gets an ordinary lease from a network stack compiled into the emulator; packets terminate there and become framed sessions carried by a Worker that is itself the tailnet node — with window credit for backpressure and an ACL test that proves whose identity is on the wire.

chapters.title: Freeze the Machine, Restore It Anywhere
chapters.blurb: A running machine serialized into a tagged container with zero-elided RAM, locked to its build, kernel and overlay generation, streamed into IndexedDB a megabyte at a time — so a page load restores in about a second instead of executing a forty-second Linux boot.

chapters.title: Rewind: The Machine Is a Stream
chapters.blurb: Why a snapshot per instruction is 100 TB/s of nonsense and keyframes-plus-a-log is the real design — then the log grows up into a durable stream: the agent's actions recorded beside the interrupts, the whole operating system suspendable at any instruction, live replicas on every subscribed tailnet device, and record-and-replay time travel for kernel, filesystem, and agent at once.

chapters.title: A Cluster Only You Can Read
chapters.blurb: The tailnet torrent gains a control plane stolen from IPFS — provider-record gossip, pinning upgraded to a reconciled replication spec, parity striped across disposable tabs — and then the same machinery turns on the private half: overlay writes and snapshots compressed, encrypted with a key only your devices hold, and erasure-sharded across peers that store unreadable noise. Any four shards restore your machine anywhere.
